sentences.text:
The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 24.05.2022 at about 7.00 p.m. Y.R.Chinmayi had been standing on left side of AnchepalyaKempanahalli Road infront of her house at Yaliyuru Village,
Huthridurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumakur District, a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA06 HG8541 came at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against her, due to the impact of the accident, she sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.

Immediately after the accident, body was taken to CHC, Kunigal wherein post mortem was conducted and petitioners have performed funeral ceremony by spending Rs.80,000/ and Rs.20,000/ for transportation charges.

3. At the time of accident, deceased/Y.R.Chinmayi was aged about 20 years, hale and healthy, he was tailoring work, thereby earning SCCH5 Rs.20,000/ p.m., due to the sudden death of Y.R.Chinmayi, they have lost love and affection of the deceased, they are under physical and mental pain, which cannot be compensated by any means.
Out of this accident crime No.171/2022 is registered against the rider of the said motor cycle before the Kuigal Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC.
R1 is owner, R2 is insurer of the said motor cycle, they jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, R1/owner has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioners, he is R.C.Owner of the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA06HG8541, the said vehicle is insured with SCCH5 R2 bearing policy No.3397/00968208/000/00 valid 28.01.2020 to 27.01.2025, hence insurance policy was valid as on the date of accident.
Further rider of the said motor cycle had valid driving license as on the date of accident vide D.L.No.KA0620190013583.
Claim made by the petitioners is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has deposed her evidence as PW1, in her chiefexamination she has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

10.
The counsel for R1/owner has not cross examined the PW1, only counsel for R2/insurer has crossexamined the PW1, wherein he has not denied place, date and time of the accident.
As per his SCCH5 suggestion very accident is occurred in middle of the road, but as per say of the petitioners very accident is occurred on footpath.
As per averments of the petition, deceased was standing on left side of the Anchepalya Kempanahalli road.
In chiefexamination also PW1 has stated the said aspect.
In the case on hand, PW1 is not a eyewitness.

11. There is no dispute about cause of the accident by the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA06HG 8541, but defence is that, there is contributory negligence of the deceased and the rider of the motor cycle by name Puneeth N.

The charge sheet speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the motor cyclists, but hand sketch map marked at Ex.P.4 speaks that, it is a straight road and very accident is occurred on SCCH5 the public road, further this accident is not occurred on footpath as per say of the petitioner in her cross examination.
It is noticed that, very road is not a highway road, it is only a double road, footpath is in existence.
Under such circumstances, deceased would have moved through the footpath, but she went on public road at about 7.00 p.m. on 24.05.2022, hence this accident is occurred.
Further there is suggestion that, very motor cycle bearing Reg.No. KA06HG8541 has not caused this accident.

One TVS vehicle has caused this accident, but such suggestions are denied by the PW1.
12.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence by the counsel for R2.
R1 has filed written statement but not at all contested the petition.
Under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that, SCCH5 very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the motor cycle by name Puneeth N.
So that, I have answered the above issue No.1 in the affirmative.

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased Y.R.Chinmayi was aged about 20 years at the time of accident.
